elements.quote: We performed this study to summarize the evidence about the use of SB in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA).
elements.reason: The abstract describes the study as a summary of evidence, and the title explicitly states it is a systematic review and meta-analysis.

elements.quote: We performed this study to summarize the evidence about the use of SB in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA).
elements.reason: The objective is clearly stated in the abstract.

elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Scopus, EBSCO, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library, until June 2019, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies that used SB in patients with OHCA.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the study design (RCTs and observational studies) and population (adult patients with OHCA), but does not explicitly list exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Scopus, EBSCO, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library, until June 2019

elements.quote: Odds ratio (OR) with their 95% confidence interval (CI) were pooled in a random or fixed meta-analysis model.

elements.quote: A total of 14 studies (four RCTs and 10 observational studies) enrolling 28,412 patients were included; of them, eight studies were included in the meta-analysis.

elements.quote: The overall pooled estimate did not favor SB or control in terms of survival rate at discharge (OR= 0.66, 95% CI [0.18, 2.44], p =0.53) and ROSC rate (OR= 1.54, 95% CI [0.38, 6.27], p =0.54), while the pooled estimate of two studies showed that SB was associated with less sustained ROSC (OR= 0.27, 95% CI [0.07, 0.98], p =0.045) and good neurological outcomes at discharge (OR= 0.12, 95% CI [0.09, 0.15], p <0.01).
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes.

elements.quote: The overall pooled estimate did not favor SB or control in terms of survival rate at discharge (OR= 0.66, 95% CI [0.18, 2.44], p =0.53) and ROSC rate (OR= 1.54, 95% CI [0.38, 6.27], p =0.54), while the pooled estimate of two studies showed that SB was associated with less sustained ROSC (OR= 0.27, 95% CI [0.07, 0.98], p =0.045) and good neurological outcomes at discharge (OR= 0.12, 95% CI [0.09, 0.15], p <0.01).

elements.quote: Conclusion: The current evidence demonstrated that SB was not superior to the control group in terms of survival to discharge and return of spontaneous circulation. Further, SB was associated with lower rates of sustained ROSC and good neurological outcomes.

elements.quote: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a common cause of death worldwide (Neumar et al., Circulation 122:S729 - S767, 2010), affecting about 300,000 persons in the USA on an annual basis; 92% of them die (Roger et al., Circulation 123:e18 - e209, 2011). The existing evidence about the use of sodium bicarbonate (SB) for the treatment of cardiac arrest is controversial.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly describes the burden of OHCA and notes that the existing evidence regarding the use of sodium bicarbonate is controversial, establishing the current state of knowledge and uncertainty.

elements.quote: We performed this study to summarize the evidence about the use of SB in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA).
elements.reason: The authors state the purpose of the study is to summarize the evidence, which explains the need for the review in light of the previously mentioned controversy.
There is no evidence provided that this is an update or replication of a specific previous systematic review, so this requirement does not apply.

The intervention (sodium bicarbonate administration) is a pharmacological treatment and not a complex intervention or delivery context requiring a logic model.
